records.source: וּבְיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֗ה נֶאֶסְפ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּצ֣וֹם וּבְשַׂקִּ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And on day twenty and four of the month the this were gathered the sons of Israel with fasting and in sackcloths, and earth [was] on them.
pieces: On the twenty-fourth day of this month the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gathered together, fasting, dressed in sackcloth, and with dust on their heads.

L.1: And on the twenty-fourth day of this month the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were gathered with fasting and in sackcloth, and [with] earth on them.

R.1: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} met together again. They went without food, wore rough clothes made of sackcloth and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth day of this month: two days after the Festival of Booths ended
decisions.reason: The festival ran from the fifteenth to the twenty-second day of the seventh month (8:14, 18; Leviticus 23:34-36). The grief that was held back on the holy days (8:9-11) is now given its time.

decisions.choice: fasting, sackcloth and earth: signs of mourning and repentance
decisions.reason: Going without food, wearing rough cloth of goat hair and putting dust or earth on the head were ways of showing grief and humbling oneself before God (Joshua 7:6; 1 Samuel 4:12; Jonah 3:5-8; Daniel 9:3). The Hebrew says only "earth on them"; it was put on the head (2 Samuel 1:2; 15:32).

decisions.choice: dust on their heads
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the earth was put, as the custom shows; Readable also says what the signs meant.

records.heading: A day of fasting and confession

records.source: וַיִּבָּֽדְלוּ֙ זֶ֣רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִכֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָ֑ר וַיַּעַמְד֗וּ וַיִּתְוַדּוּ֙ עַל־חַטֹּ֣אתֵיהֶ֔ם וַעֲוֺנ֖וֹת אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And separated themselves [the] seed of Israel from all sons of foreignness, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
pieces: Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all foreigners. They stood and confessed their sins and the wrongs of their ancestors.

L.2: And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

R.2: The people who were born Israelites kept apart from all the foreigners. They stood up and admitted the sins they had done and the wrong things their ancestors had done.

decisions.choice: the seed of Israel: those descended from Israel
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring, descendants (Ezra 9:2; Isaiah 41:8). The phrase sets those who belonged to Israel by birth apart from the foreigners living among them.

decisions.choice: separated themselves from all foreigners: a day of confession for Israel alone
decisions.reason: The day was set apart for Israel to confess its own and its ancestors' sins, which outsiders did not share. Elsewhere the separation is from the worship and the marriages that the law forbade (Ezra 6:21; 9:1-2; 10:11; Nehemiah 10:29-31; 13:3). The text does not say that foreigners who had joined themselves to the LORD were sent away; 10:29 counts among the people "everyone who separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God".

decisions.choice: confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers
decisions.reason: The people own both their own sins and the long history of their ancestors' unfaithfulness, which the prayer that follows tells (verses 16-18, 26-30, 34-35). Confessing the ancestors' sins as one's own is what Leviticus 26:40 asks of a people in exile (compare Daniel 9:5-11).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", which here means the earlier generations as a whole; Literal keeps "fathers".

records.source: וַיָּק֨וּמוּ֙ עַל־עָמְדָ֔ם וַֽיִּקְרְא֗וּ בְּסֵ֨פֶר תּוֹרַ֧ת יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם רְבִעִ֣ית הַיּ֑וֹם וּרְבִעִית֙ מִתְוַדִּ֣ים וּמִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֔ים לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And they stood on their place and they read in [the] book of [the] law of YHWH their God a fourth of the day, and a fourth [they were] confessing and bowing down to YHWH their God.
pieces: They stood in their places and read from the book of the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God for a quarter of the day, and for another quarter they confessed their sins and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

L.3: And they stood in their place and read in the book of the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God for a fourth of the day, and for [another] fourth they were confessing and bowing down to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

R.3: They stood in their places while the book of the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God was read for about three hours. Then for about three more hours they admitted their sins and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: a fourth of the day: about three hours
decisions.reason: The daylight hours were counted as about twelve (John 11:9), so a quarter of the day was about three hours. The reading and the confession took up much of the day.

decisions.choice: bowing down: worshiping
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low to the ground in worship (8:6).

decisions.choice: about three hours
decisions.reason: Readable turns the Hebrew way of counting the day into hours, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: וַיָּ֜קָם עַֽל־מַֽעֲלֵ֣ה הַלְוִיִּ֗ם יֵשׁ֨וּעַ וּבָנִ֜י קַדְמִיאֵ֧ל שְׁבַנְיָ֛ה בֻּנִּ֥י שֵׁרֵבְיָ֖ה בָּנִ֣י כְנָ֑נִי וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And stood on [the] ascent of the Levites Jeshua and Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, Kenani, and they cried with a voice great to YHWH their God.
pieces: On the Levites' platform stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Kenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

L.4: And on the stairs of the Levites stood Jeshua and Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, [and] Kenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

R.4: Some Levites stood on a raised place built for them: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Kenani. They called out loudly to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: the ascent of the Levites: a raised place or stairs where the Levites stood
decisions.reason: The word means a way up, steps or stairs (1 Kings 10:19; Ezekiel 40:6). It was a raised place, perhaps steps or a platform, from which the Levites led the people, as Ezra did from his platform in 8:4.

decisions.choice: eight Levites, two named Bani
decisions.reason: The list names Bani twice; they may be two men of the same name, or the text may have repeated a name. Several of these Levites appear again in verse 5 and among those who seal the covenant (10:10-14).

decisions.choice: platform; a raised place
decisions.reason: Balanced says "platform" and Readable "a raised place", what the steps were for; Literal keeps "ascent".

records.heading: The Levites lead the people in prayer

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ הַלְוִיִּ֡ם יֵשׁ֣וּעַ וְ֠קַדְמִיאֵל בָּנִ֨י חֲשַׁבְנְיָ֜ה שֵׁרֵֽבְיָ֤ה הֽוֹדִיָּה֙ שְׁבַנְיָ֣ה פְתַֽחְיָ֔ה ק֗וּמוּ בָּרֲכוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם מִן־הָעוֹלָ֖ם עַד־הָעוֹלָ֑ם וִיבָֽרְכוּ֙ שֵׁ֣ם כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ וּמְרוֹמַ֥ם עַל־כָּל־בְּרָכָ֖ה וּתְהִלָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said the Levites, Jeshua and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, Pethahiah, Stand up, bless YHWH your God from the everlasting until the everlasting; and may they bless [the] name of ~your glory, and [it is] exalted above all blessing and praise.
pieces: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, from everlasting to everlasting! May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glorious name be blessed, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.

L.5: And the Levites, Jeshua and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, [and] Pethahiah, said, "Stand up, bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God from everlasting to everlasting. And may they bless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.

R.5: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who lives forever and ever!" Then they prayed, "May everyone praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonderful name! It is far greater than any praise or blessing we could give.

decisions.choice: the call to the people turns into praise addressed to God
decisions.reason: "Bless the LORD your God" speaks to the people; "your glorious name" speaks to God. The Levites' call to worship passes straight into the prayer that runs to verse 37, which is spoken to God throughout.

decisions.choice: from everlasting to everlasting: for all time, past and future
decisions.reason: The phrase means forever in both directions, without beginning or end (Psalm 41:14; 90:2; 106:48; 1 Chronicles 16:36).

decisions.choice: may they bless: may your name be blessed
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it is a wish that God's name be praised by all.

decisions.choice: the name of your glory: your glorious name
decisions.reason: In Hebrew a noun can describe another noun this way ("name of glory" means "glorious name"). God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known (Exodus 34:5-7).

decisions.choice: Then they prayed
decisions.reason: Readable marks where the call to the people becomes a prayer to God, as the grammar decision explains.

records.source: אַתָּה־ה֣וּא יְהוָה֮ לְבַדֶּךָ֒ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֡יתָ אֶֽת־הַשָּׁמַיִם֩ שְׁמֵ֨י הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וְכָל־צְבָאָ֗ם הָאָ֜רֶץ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ הַיַּמִּים֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּהֶ֔ם וְאַתָּ֖ה מְחַיֶּ֣ה אֶת־כֻּלָּ֑ם וּצְבָ֥א הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לְךָ֥ מִשְׁתַּחֲוִֽים׃
records.gloss: You [are] he, YHWH, you alone; you made the heavens, [the] heavens of the heavens and all their host, the earth and all that [is] on it, the seas and all that [is] in them; and you preserve alive all of them, and [the] host of the heavens to you [are] bowing down.
pieces: You alone are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to all of them, and the host of heaven worships {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.6: You [are] he, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made the heavens, the heavens of the heavens and all their host, the earth and all that [is] on it, the seas and all that [is] in them; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep all of them alive, and the host of the heavens bows down to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.6: You alone are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You made the skies and the highest heavens and everything that fills them. You made the earth and everything on it, and the seas and everything in them. You keep them all alive, and all the beings of heaven worship {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: the prayer is not given a speaker in the Hebrew; the ancient Greek translation adds "And Ezra said"
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text the prayer follows the Levites' call in verse 5 with no new speaker, so it reads as the Levites' prayer on behalf of the people. The Greek translation (the Septuagint) begins verse 6 with "And Ezra said". The Hebrew text is followed here; the Greek addition may be an early reader's attempt to name the one who led the prayer.

decisions.choice: "You are he, the LORD, you alone": an emphatic confession that only the LORD is God
decisions.reason: "You are he" is a strong way of saying "you are the one" (Isaiah 43:10, 13; Psalm 102:28). With "you alone" the prayer opens by confessing that there is no other God (Deuteronomy 4:35, 39; 2 Kings 19:15, 19).

decisions.choice: the heavens of the heavens; host: the highest heavens and all that fills them
decisions.reason: "The heavens of the heavens" is the Hebrew way of saying the highest heavens (Deuteronomy 10:14; 1 Kings 8:27). "Their host" first means the sun, moon and stars, the array that fills the sky (Genesis 2:1; Deuteronomy 4:19). "The host of the heavens" that bows down to God is the company of heavenly beings who worship him (Psalm 103:20-21; 148:2).

decisions.choice: preserve alive: give life to and keep alive
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative form of "live": God gives life and keeps it going (Job 12:10; Psalm 36:7). The creator is also the one who sustains all things.

decisions.choice: the skies; everything that fills them; the beings of heaven
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the old word "host" and explains what is meant, following the decision on those words.

records.source: אַתָּה־הוּא֙ יְהוָ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתָּ֙ בְּאַבְרָ֔ם וְהוֹצֵאת֖וֹ מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וְשַׂ֥מְתָּ שְּׁמ֖וֹ אַבְרָהָֽם׃
records.gloss: You [are] he, YHWH the God, who chose Abram and brought him out from Ur of [the] Chaldeans and made his name Abraham.
pieces: You are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.

L.7: You [are] he, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.

R.7: You are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God. You chose Abram and brought him out of the city of Ur in the land of the Chaldeans. You gave him a new name, Abraham.

decisions.choice: chose Abram, brought him out of Ur, named him Abraham: Genesis 11:31-12:3; 15:7; 17:5
decisions.reason: The prayer retells Israel's history from its beginning. God called Abram (Genesis 12:1-3), brought him out of Ur (Genesis 15:7, where God says "I am the LORD who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans", the same words used here), and changed his name to Abraham, "father of a multitude" (Genesis 17:5).

decisions.choice: Ur of the Chaldeans: an ancient city in southern Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: Ur lay near the Euphrates in what is now southern Iraq. The Chaldeans were the people of that region, who later ruled Babylon; the name tells later readers where Ur was (Genesis 11:28, 31).

decisions.choice: the city of Ur in the land of the Chaldeans; a new name
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Ur was a city and that "Abraham" was a new name, as Genesis 17:5 tells.

records.source: וּמָצָ֣אתָ אֶת־לְבָבוֹ֮ נֶאֱמָ֣ן לְפָנֶיךָ֒ וְכָר֨וֹת עִמּ֜וֹ הַבְּרִ֗ית לָתֵ֡ת אֶת־אֶרֶץ֩ הַכְּנַעֲנִ֨י הַחִתִּ֜י הָאֱמֹרִ֧י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֛י וְהַיְבוּסִ֥י וְהַגִּרְגָּשִׁ֖י לָתֵ֣ת לְזַרְע֑וֹ וַתָּ֨קֶם֙ אֶת־דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י צַדִּ֖יק אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: And you found his heart faithful before you, and you made with him the covenant to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give [it] to his seed; and you established your words, for righteous [are] you.
pieces: You found his heart faithful before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites and the Girgashites, to give it to his descendants. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are righteous.

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} found his heart faithful before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made with him the covenant to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give [it] to his seed; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have established {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] righteous.

R.8: You saw that his heart was faithful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made a covenant with him. You promised to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites and Girgashites. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are righteous.

decisions.choice: you found his heart faithful and made the covenant: Genesis 15:6, 18-21
decisions.reason: "Faithful" comes from the same root as the verb in Genesis 15:6, "Abram believed the LORD". In the same chapter God made a covenant with Abram to give his descendants the land, listing the peoples who lived in it (Genesis 15:18-21). The list here gives six of those peoples.

decisions.choice: established your words: you kept your promise
decisions.reason: To "establish" or "make stand" a word is to carry it out (Deuteronomy 9:5; 1 Kings 8:20). The prayer says God did what he had promised Abraham: Israel received the land (verses 22-25).

decisions.choice: for you are righteous
decisions.reason: God's righteousness here is his faithfulness to his own word and his rightness in all he does. The prayer comes back to it in verse 33: whatever has happened to Israel, God has been in the right.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites, the Hittites ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names each people in the singular as a group ("the Canaanite"); English uses the plural.

records.source: וַתֵּ֛רֶא אֶת־עֳנִ֥י אֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־זַעֲקָתָ֥ם שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ עַל־יַם־סֽוּף׃
records.gloss: And you saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and their cry you heard at [the] Sea of Reeds.
pieces: You saw the suffering of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} heard their cry at the Sea of Reeds.

R.9: You saw how our ancestors suffered in Egypt. You heard them cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at the Red Sea.

decisions.choice: you saw the affliction ... heard their cry: Exodus 3:7; 14:10
decisions.reason: The words echo what God said to Moses at the burning bush: "I have surely seen the affliction of my people in Egypt and have heard their cry" (Exodus 3:7). At the sea the Israelites cried out to the LORD when Pharaoh's army came near (Exodus 14:10).

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name means "sea of reeds". The ancient Greek translation called it the Red Sea, the name by which it has long been known.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, "fathers" means the earlier generations; Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds (Literal); the Red Sea (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the meaning of the Hebrew name, as in Exodus 15:4; Balanced and Readable use the familiar English name.

records.source: וַ֠תִּתֵּן אֹתֹ֨ת וּמֹֽפְתִ֜ים בְּפַרְעֹ֤ה וּבְכָל־עֲבָדָיו֙ וּבְכָל־עַ֣ם אַרְצ֔וֹ כִּ֣י יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּ֥י הֵזִ֖ידוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתַּֽעַשׂ־לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כְּהַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And you gave signs and wonders on Pharaoh and on all his servants and on all [the] people of his land, for you knew that they acted presumptuously against them; and you made for yourself a name as [at] the day the this.
pieces: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his officials and against all the people of his land, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} knew how arrogantly they had treated our ancestors. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made a name for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} that remains to this day.

L.10: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave signs and wonders against Pharaoh and against all his servants and against all the people of his land, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} knew that they acted presumptuously against them; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} a name, as [it is] this day.

R.10: You did miraculous signs and wonders to punish Pharaoh, his officials and all the people of his land. You knew how proudly and cruelly they had treated our ancestors. That is how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name famous, as it still is today.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders against Pharaoh: the plagues of Egypt
decisions.reason: "Signs and wonders" names the plagues and the deliverance from Egypt (Exodus 7:3; Deuteronomy 4:34; 6:22; Psalm 135:9).

decisions.choice: acted presumptuously against them: treated them with arrogance
decisions.reason: The verb means to act proudly, to set oneself up against another (Exodus 18:11, where Jethro says the LORD is greater than all gods "in the very thing in which they acted proudly against them"). "Them" means Israel. The same verb is used of Israel itself in verses 16 and 29.

decisions.choice: you made a name for yourself: you made yourself known and honored
decisions.reason: A "name" here means fame and honor. Through the exodus God became known among the nations (Exodus 9:16; Isaiah 63:12, 14). "As it is this day" means it is still so.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court officials, as the term table has it; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whom "them" refers to, so the reader does not take it to mean the Egyptians.

records.source: וְהַיָּם֙ בָּקַ֣עְתָּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ־הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְֽאֶת־רֹ֨דְפֵיהֶ֜ם הִשְׁלַ֧כְתָּ בִמְצוֹלֹ֛ת כְּמוֹ־אֶ֖בֶן בְּמַ֥יִם עַזִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And the sea you split before them, and they passed in [the] midst of the sea on the dry ground; and their pursuers you threw into [the] depths like a stone into waters mighty.
pieces: You split the sea open before them, and they went through the middle of the sea on dry ground. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hurled their pursuers into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} split the sea before them, and they passed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} threw their pursuers into the depths like a stone into mighty waters.

R.11: You split the sea in two in front of them, and they walked through the middle of it on dry ground. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} threw the soldiers who were chasing them into the deep sea. They sank like a stone in the powerful waters.

decisions.choice: the sea split, the pursuers thrown into the depths like a stone: Exodus 14:21-29; 15:5, 10
decisions.reason: The prayer uses the words of the exodus story and the song at the sea: the waters were split, Israel went through on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22), and the Egyptians "went down into the depths like a stone" and "sank like lead in the mighty waters" (Exodus 15:5, 10).

decisions.choice: the soldiers who were chasing them
decisions.reason: Readable says who the pursuers were: Pharaoh's army (Exodus 14:9, 23).

records.source: וּבְעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן הִנְחִיתָ֖ם יוֹמָ֑ם וּבְעַמּ֥וּד אֵשׁ֙ לַ֔יְלָה לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם אֶת־הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And with a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and with a pillar of fire [by] night, to light for them the way in which they should walk.
pieces: By day {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led them with a pillar of cloud, and by night with a pillar of fire, to light up the way for them in which they should go.

L.12: And with a pillar of cloud {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led them by day, and with a pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way in which they should go.

R.12: In the daytime {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led them with a tall column of cloud. At night {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led them with a column of fire. It gave them light to show them the way they should go.

decisions.choice: a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night: Exodus 13:21-22
decisions.reason: God went before Israel in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, so they could travel by day and by night (Exodus 13:21-22; Numbers 14:14). The prayer returns to it in verse 19.

decisions.choice: a tall column of cloud
decisions.reason: Readable explains "pillar" as a tall column, the shape of the cloud.

records.source: וְעַ֤ל הַר־סִינַי֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ וְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּהֶ֖ם מִשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם מִשְׁפָּטִ֤ים יְשָׁרִים֙ וְתוֹר֣וֹת אֱמֶ֔ת חֻקִּ֥ים וּמִצְוֺ֖ת טוֹבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And on Mount Sinai you came down and you spoke with them from heaven and you gave to them judgments upright and laws of truth, statutes and commandments good.
pieces: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them right rulings and true laws, good statutes and commandments.

L.13: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them upright judgments and laws of truth, good statutes and commandments.

R.13: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven. You gave them rules that are fair, teachings that are true, and good laws and commands.

decisions.choice: you came down on Mount Sinai and spoke from heaven: Exodus 19:18-20; 20:22
decisions.reason: The LORD came down on the mountain in fire (Exodus 19:18-20), and he spoke to Israel from heaven (Exodus 20:22; Deuteronomy 4:36). The prayer keeps both.

decisions.choice: judgments, laws, statutes and commandments: the whole of God's instruction
decisions.reason: The four words name the law from different sides: rulings for justice, teachings, fixed decrees and commands (Deuteronomy 4:8; Psalm 19:8-10). "Laws of truth" means true, reliable instruction. Together the words say that all of it was right and good.

decisions.choice: rules, teachings, laws and commands
decisions.reason: Readable follows the term table for these words (laws, rules, commands) and says "teachings" for the plural of the word "law", which means instruction.

records.source: וְאֶת־שַׁבַּ֥ת קָדְשְׁךָ֖ הוֹדַ֣עַתָלָהֶ֑ם וּמִצְו֤וֹת וְחֻקִּים֙ וְתוֹרָ֔ה צִוִּ֣יתָ לָהֶ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And your sabbath of holiness you made known to them, and commandments and statutes and law you commanded to them by [the] hand of Moses your slave.
pieces: You made known to them {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy Sabbath, and through Moses {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded them commandments, statutes and law.

L.14: And {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made known to them, and commandments and statutes and law {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded them through Moses {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave.

R.14: You taught them to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy day of rest, the Sabbath. Through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them commands, laws and teachings.

decisions.choice: you made known your holy Sabbath: the Sabbath as God's gift and sign
decisions.reason: The Sabbath is named on its own, apart from the other commandments, because it was the sign of the covenant between God and Israel (Exodus 31:13-17; Ezekiel 20:12). It was made known in the wilderness (Exodus 16:23-30) and at Sinai (Exodus 20:8-11). Keeping the Sabbath is a matter the people take up again in 10:32 and 13:15-22.

decisions.choice: Moses your servant: Moses as God's servant
decisions.reason: The word means a slave or servant; "the servant of the LORD" is Moses' title of honor (Numbers 12:7; Deuteronomy 34:5; Joshua 1:1). It speaks of Moses' position as one wholly at his master's service.

decisions.choice: through Moses your servant you commanded them
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "through Moses" first so that the list of what was commanded ends the sentence.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: By the style guide's rule for this word: Literal keeps "slave", Balanced and Readable say "servant", Moses' title of honor.

records.source: וְ֠לֶחֶם מִשָּׁמַ֜יִם נָתַ֤תָּה לָהֶם֙ לִרְעָבָ֔ם וּמַ֗יִם מִסֶּ֛לַע הוֹצֵ֥אתָ לָהֶ֖ם לִצְמָאָ֑ם וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם לָבוֹא֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נָשָׂ֥אתָ אֶת־יָדְךָ֖ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And bread from heaven you gave to them for their hunger, and water from a rock you brought out for them for their thirst; and you said to them to go in to possess the land which you had lifted your hand to give to them.
pieces: You gave them bread from heaven when they were hungry, and brought water out of the rock for them when they were thirsty. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told them to go in and take possession of the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had sworn to give them.

L.15: And bread from heaven {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them for their hunger, and water from the rock {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought out for them for their thirst; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told them to go in to take possession of the land which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had lifted {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand to give them.

R.15: When they were hungry, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them bread from heaven. When they were thirsty, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought water out of a rock for them. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told them to go in and take the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had promised with an oath to give them.

decisions.choice: bread from heaven, water from the rock: Exodus 16:4; 17:6; Numbers 20:8-11
decisions.reason: The manna is called bread from heaven (Exodus 16:4; Psalm 78:24; 105:40). Water came out of the rock at Horeb (Exodus 17:6) and at Kadesh (Numbers 20:8-11).

decisions.choice: lifted your hand: swore an oath
decisions.reason: Raising the hand was the gesture of one taking an oath, so "lift the hand" means "swear" (Exodus 6:8; Numbers 14:30; Ezekiel 20:5-6).

decisions.choice: to possess: to take possession of the land as an inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over and hold a land, often by driving out those who held it (Deuteronomy 1:8). It returns in verses 22-25.

records.source: וְהֵ֥ם וַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ הֵזִ֑ידוּ וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־עָרְפָּ֔ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And they and our fathers acted presumptuously, and they stiffened their neck and did not listen to your commandments.
pieces: But they, our ancestors, acted arrogantly. They stiffened their necks and would not obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments.

L.16: But they, our fathers, acted presumptuously; they stiffened their neck and did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments.

R.16: But our ancestors became proud and stubborn. They refused to obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.choice: "they and our fathers": they, that is, our fathers
decisions.reason: The "and" here most likely explains "they" ("they, our fathers"), as Hebrew "and" sometimes does; the prayer is speaking of the same generation as in verses 9-15. It could also add the later generations to the wilderness generation. Either way, the prayer turns here from God's goodness to Israel's sin.

decisions.choice: stiffened their neck: became stubborn
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that will not bend its neck to the yoke. It is said of Israel from the golden calf on (Exodus 32:9; 33:3; Deuteronomy 9:6; 2 Kings 17:14).

decisions.choice: did not listen to: did not obey
decisions.reason: "Listen to" in Hebrew often means to obey (Exodus 19:5; Deuteronomy 11:13).

decisions.choice: proud and stubborn
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the stiff neck and the arrogance of verse 16 in plain words.

records.source: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לִשְׁמֹ֗עַ וְלֹא־זָכְר֤וּ נִפְלְאֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּהֶ֔ם וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־עָרְפָּ֔ם וַיִּתְּנוּ־רֹ֛אשׁ לָשׁ֥וּב לְעַבְדֻתָ֖ם בְּמִרְיָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֩ אֱל֨וֹהַּ סְלִיח֜וֹת חַנּ֧וּן וְרַח֛וּם אֶֽרֶךְ־אַפַּ֥יִם וְרַב־חֶ֖סֶדוְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And they refused to listen, and did not remember your wonders which you had done with them, and they stiffened their neck and gave a head to return to their slavery in their rebellion; and you [are] a God of forgivenesses, gracious and compassionate, long of anger and great of steadfast love, and you did not forsake them.
pieces: They refused to listen and did not remember the wonders {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had done among them. They stiffened their necks and in their rebellion appointed a leader to go back to their slavery. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a God who forgives, gracious and full of compassion, slow to become angry and rich in faithful love, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not abandon them.

L.17: And they refused to listen and did not remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had done among them; and they stiffened their neck and appointed a head to return to their slavery in their rebellion. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in steadfast love, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not forsake them.

R.17: They refused to listen. They forgot the wonderful things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had done for them. They became stubborn, and in their rebellion they chose a leader to take them back to being slaves. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a God who forgives. You are kind and full of mercy. You are slow to become angry, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love is great. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not leave them.

decisions.choice: "in their rebellion"; some manuscripts read "in Egypt"
alternatives: to return to their slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "in their rebellion". The ancient Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts read "in Egypt"; the two Hebrew words look alike. The phrase recalls Numbers 14:4, where the people said, "Let us appoint a head and return to Egypt." The text here follows the standard Hebrew text, which makes good sense: the plan to go back was itself an act of rebellion.

decisions.choice: appointed a head to return to their slavery: Numbers 14:4
decisions.reason: After the spies' report the people said, "Let us appoint a head and return to Egypt" (Numbers 14:4). The prayer calls going back to Egypt by its true name: a return to slavery.

decisions.choice: a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in steadfast love: Exodus 34:6-7
decisions.reason: These are the words in which the LORD proclaimed his own name to Moses after the golden calf (Exodus 34:6-7). Israel repeats them in its prayers (Numbers 14:18; Psalm 86:15; 103:8; Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2). "Long of anger" means slow to become angry. The word translated "steadfast love" is God's loyal, faithful love to those bound to him by covenant.

decisions.choice: a God of forgivenesses: a God who is ready to forgive
decisions.reason: The plural "forgivenesses" says that forgiveness belongs to God's nature and is given again and again (Psalm 130:4; Daniel 9:9). The word for God here is the singular form often used in Job and poetry.

decisions.choice: slavery
decisions.reason: The word means the state of a slave. It refers to Israel's slavery in Egypt, so it stays "slavery" at every level, as the style guide asks.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the term table, Balanced and Readable say "faithful love", Literal "steadfast love".

records.source: אַ֗ף כִּֽי־עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֶלְךָ֖ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Even when they made for themselves a calf of cast metal and said, This [is] your god who brought you up from Egypt, and did great blasphemies,
pieces: Even when they made for themselves a calf of cast metal and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies,

L.18: Even when they had made for themselves a calf of cast metal and said, 'This [is] your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and had done great blasphemies,

R.18: They even made a metal statue of a calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you out of Egypt!' They did terrible things that insulted {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: a calf of cast metal: the golden calf at Sinai, Exodus 32:4
decisions.reason: At Sinai Aaron made a calf of melted gold, and the people said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt" (Exodus 32:4, 8). The prayer gives the words in the singular, "This is your god", since there was only one calf; the Hebrew word for God and gods is the same.

decisions.choice: blasphemies: acts of contempt toward God
decisions.reason: The word means acts or words that scorn and despise God (Numbers 14:11, 23 use the verb; Ezekiel 35:12). The same phrase returns in verse 26.

decisions.choice: Even when ... : the sentence goes on into verse 19
decisions.reason: Verse 18 is a clause of concession; its main clause is verse 19, "you in your great compassion did not forsake them".

decisions.choice: the verse ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 19. Readable makes verse 18 its own sentences and begins verse 19 with "But even then".

decisions.choice: that insulted you
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the blasphemies were by saying whom they scorned.

records.source: וְאַתָּה֙ בְּרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים לֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר אֶת־עַמּ֣וּד הֶ֠עָנָן לֹא־סָ֨ר מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֤ם בְּיוֹמָם֙ לְהַנְחֹתָ֣ם בְּהַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת־עַמּ֨וּד הָאֵ֤שׁ בְּלַ֨יְלָה֙ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: you in your compassions the great did not forsake them in the wilderness; the pillar of the cloud did not depart from over them by day to lead them in the way, and the pillar of the fire by night to light for them the way in which they should walk.
pieces: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not leave them by day, to lead them on their way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to light up the way they should go.

L.19: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not turn away from them by day, to lead them in the way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way in which they should go.

R.19: But even then, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mercy is so great, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not leave them alone in the wilderness. In the daytime the column of cloud kept leading them on their way. At night the column of fire kept lighting up the road for them.

decisions.choice: compassions: deep, tender mercy
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for a mother's womb, and means the deep pity one feels for one's own (Psalm 103:13; Isaiah 49:15). The plural strengthens it. It returns in verses 27, 28 and 31.

decisions.choice: the pillar did not depart: Exodus 13:22; Numbers 14:14
decisions.reason: Even after the calf, God kept going with Israel (Exodus 33:14-17), and the pillar of cloud and fire did not leave them (Exodus 13:22; 40:36-38).

decisions.choice: kept leading; kept lighting
decisions.reason: Readable turns "did not depart from over them" into a plain positive statement with the same meaning.

records.source: וְרוּחֲךָ֨ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה נָתַ֖תָּ לְהַשְׂכִּילָ֑ם וּמַנְךָ֙ לֹא־מָנַ֣עְתָּ מִפִּיהֶ֔ם וּמַ֛יִם נָתַ֥תָּה לָהֶ֖ם לִצְמָאָֽם׃
records.gloss: And your spirit the good you gave to instruct them, and your manna you did not withhold from their mouth, and water you gave to them for their thirst.
pieces: You gave {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} good Spirit to instruct them. You did not hold back {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} manna from their mouths, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them water for their thirst.

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} good Spirit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to instruct them, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} manna {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not withhold from their mouth, and water {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them for their thirst.

R.20: You gave {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} good Spirit to teach them. You did not stop giving them manna to eat, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them water when they were thirsty.

decisions.choice: your good Spirit: God's own Spirit, given to guide Israel
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks of God's Spirit at work among Israel in the wilderness: he put his Spirit on the seventy elders (Numbers 11:17, 25), and Isaiah 63:11-14 speaks of the holy Spirit set among them in Moses' time. "Your good Spirit" is used in Psalm 143:10 for the Spirit who leads. The word can also mean wind or breath, but here it is God's Spirit who teaches.

decisions.choice: manna: the food God gave in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Manna was the bread from heaven of verse 15 (Exodus 16:31, 35; Numbers 11:7-9). The Israelites gave it its name, which sounds like their question "What is it?" (Exodus 16:15).

decisions.choice: Spirit, with a capital S
decisions.reason: English capitalizes the word because it means God's own Spirit, as the meaning decision says, the same way "the Spirit of the LORD" is written in Judges.

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה כִּלְכַּלְתָּ֥ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר לֹ֣א חָסֵ֑רוּ שַׂלְמֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ לֹ֣א בָל֔וּ וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א בָצֵֽקוּ׃
records.gloss: And forty years you sustained them in the wilderness; they did not lack; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
pieces: For forty years {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} provided for them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.

L.21: And forty years {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sustained them in the wilderness; they did not lack [anything]; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.

R.21: For forty years {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} took care of them in the desert. They had everything they needed. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not become swollen.

decisions.choice: forty years, lacking nothing, clothes not worn out: Deuteronomy 2:7; 8:4; 29:4
decisions.reason: Moses reminded Israel that for forty years the LORD had been with them and they had lacked nothing (Deuteronomy 2:7), that their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell (Deuteronomy 8:4; 29:4). The prayer takes up his words.

decisions.choice: sustained: provided for, fed
decisions.reason: The verb means to supply food and what is needed to live (Genesis 45:11; 1 Kings 17:4, 9).

records.source: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם מַמְלָכוֹת֙ וַעֲמָמִ֔ים וַֽתַּחְלְקֵ֖ם לְפֵאָ֑ה וַיִּֽירְשׁ֞וּ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ סִיח֗וֹן וְאֶת־אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן וְאֶת־אֶ֖רֶץ ע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: And you gave to them kingdoms and peoples, and you apportioned them to [the] corner; and they possessed the land of Sihon, and the land of [the] king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of the Bashan.
pieces: You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and allotted them every region as their share. They took possession of the land of Sihon, the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.

L.22: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them kingdoms and peoples, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} allotted them to every corner; and they took possession of the land of Sihon, that is, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.

R.22: You gave them kingdoms and nations, and divided up the land for them, every part of it. They took over the land of Sihon, the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, the king of Bashan.

decisions.choice: you apportioned them to the corner: you allotted the lands to Israel region by region
alternatives: you scattered those peoples to the far corners
you gave them land to its farthest borders
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and unclear. The verb means to share out, as land is divided by lot (Joshua 13:7; 18:2). The noun means a corner, side or border region. It most likely means that God gave Israel the conquered lands piece by piece, each part as its share. It could also mean that God drove the peoples off to the edges, or gave Israel land to its farthest border.

decisions.choice: the land of Sihon, and the land of the king of Heshbon: one land
decisions.reason: Sihon was the king of Heshbon (Numbers 21:26; Deuteronomy 2:26, 30), so the second phrase names the first again; the "and" explains, as it sometimes does in Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og: the first lands taken, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan before crossing the Jordan (Numbers 21:21-35; Deuteronomy 2:24-3:11). Their defeat became a byword for the LORD's help (Psalm 135:11; 136:19-20).

decisions.choice: allotted them every region as their share; divided up the land for them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the most likely sense, which the meaning decision marks as uncertain.

records.source: וּבְנֵיהֶ֣ם הִרְבִּ֔יתָ כְּכֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתְּבִיאֵם֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אָמַ֥רְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לָב֥וֹא לָרָֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And their sons you multiplied like the stars of the heavens, and you brought them into the land which you had said to their fathers to go in to possess.
pieces: You made their children as many as the stars of the sky, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought them into the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had told their ancestors to enter and possess.

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} multiplied their {{gender:children|sons}} like the stars of the heavens, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought them into the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had told their fathers to go in to possess.

R.23: You gave them so many descendants that they were like the stars in the sky. You brought them into the land, the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had told their ancestors to go in and take.

decisions.choice: as many as the stars of the heavens: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham that his descendants would be as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5; 22:17). Moses told Israel that the promise had come true (Deuteronomy 1:10; 10:22).

decisions.choice: their children ... their fathers: the generation that entered and the generation that had been told to enter
decisions.reason: The children are the generation that grew up in the wilderness and entered the land under Joshua. Their fathers were told to go in and possess it (Deuteronomy 1:8, 21) but refused (verse 17; Numbers 14).

decisions.choice: their children / sons
decisions.reason: The word means children of both sexes here, so Literal uses the gender setting; Balanced and Readable say "children" and "descendants", which already include everyone.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַבָּנִים֙ וַיִּֽירְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתַּכְנַ֨ע לִפְנֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֤י הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ הַכְּנַ֣עֲנִ֔ים וַֽתִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיָדָ֑ם וְאֶת־מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת־עַֽמְמֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת בָּהֶ֖ם כִּרְצוֹנָֽם׃
records.gloss: And went in the sons and possessed the land, and you subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand, and their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them according to their will.
pieces: So the children went in and took possession of the land. You subdued before them the Canaanites who lived in the land and gave them into their hands, with their kings and the peoples of the land, to deal with them as they pleased.

L.24: And the {{gender:children|sons}} went in and took possession of the land, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand, both their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they wished.

R.24: So their descendants went in and took the land. You defeated the Canaanites who lived there and made them weak in front of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. You handed them over to the Israelites, with their kings and the peoples of the land, so that the Israelites could do with them as they wanted.

decisions.choice: the children went in and possessed the land: the conquest under Joshua
decisions.reason: This sums up the book of Joshua: the LORD gave Israel the land he had sworn to their fathers (Joshua 21:43-45).

decisions.choice: subdued: brought low, humbled
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring someone down, to make them submit (Deuteronomy 9:3; Judges 4:23). It is God who humbles the Canaanites; Israel takes the land.

decisions.choice: gave them into their hand: handed them over to their power
decisions.reason: "Into the hand of" means into someone's power or control (Joshua 2:24; Judges 1:2).

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names whose hand is meant, since "their" could be read as the Canaanites'.

records.source: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֞וּ עָרִ֣ים בְּצֻרוֹת֮ וַאֲדָמָ֣ה שְׁמֵנָה֒ וַיִּֽירְשׁ֡וּ בָּתִּ֣ים מְלֵֽאִים־כָּל־ט֠וּב בֹּר֨וֹת חֲצוּבִ֜ים כְּרָמִ֧ים וְזֵיתִ֛ים וְעֵ֥ץ מַאֲכָ֖ל לָרֹ֑ב וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ וַֽיִּשְׂבְּעוּ֙ וַיַּשְׁמִ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽתְעַדְּנ֖וּ בְּטוּבְךָ֥ הַגָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And they captured cities fortified and ground fat, and they possessed houses full [of] every good [thing], cisterns hewn, vineyards and olive trees and tree[s] of food in abundance; and they ate and were satisfied and grew fat and delighted themselves in your goodness the great.
pieces: They captured fortified cities and fertile land and took possession of houses full of all good things, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves and fruit trees in plenty. They ate and were filled and grew fat, and they delighted in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great goodness.

L.25: And they captured fortified cities and fat ground and took possession of houses full of every good thing, hewn cisterns, vineyards and olive trees and fruit trees in abundance; and they ate and were satisfied and grew fat and delighted themselves in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great goodness.

R.25: They captured strong walled cities and rich farmland. They took over houses filled with good things, water pits already dug, vineyards, olive groves and many fruit trees. They ate all they wanted and grew fat. They enjoyed all the good things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great kindness.

decisions.choice: houses full of good things, cisterns, vineyards and olive trees: Deuteronomy 6:10-12
decisions.reason: Moses promised Israel houses full of good things they had not filled, cisterns they had not dug, vineyards and olive trees they had not planted, and warned them not to forget the LORD when they had eaten and were satisfied (Deuteronomy 6:10-12; 8:10-14).

decisions.choice: grew fat: well fed, and perhaps also careless
decisions.reason: The verb can simply mean they were well fed. Moses' song uses it of Israel growing fat and then forsaking God (Deuteronomy 32:15), and the next verse here tells of rebellion, so the word may already hint at what came next.

decisions.choice: hewn cisterns: water pits cut into the rock
decisions.reason: In the hill country, rain water was stored in pits cut into the rock (Deuteronomy 6:11; Jeremiah 2:13). Finding them already dug saved great labor.

decisions.choice: water pits
decisions.reason: Readable describes the cisterns, a word many readers may not know.

records.source: וַיַּמְר֨וּ וַֽיִּמְרְד֜וּ בָּ֗ךְ וַיַּשְׁלִ֤כוּ אֶת־תּוֹרָֽתְךָ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י גַוָּ֔ם וְאֶת־נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ הָרָ֔גוּ אֲשֶׁר־הֵעִ֥ידוּ בָ֖ם לַהֲשִׁיבָ֣ם אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדוֹלֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And they were disobedient and rebelled against you, and they threw your law behind their back, and your prophets they killed, who had warned them to bring them back to you; and they did great blasphemies.
pieces: But they were disobedient and rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They threw {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law behind their backs and killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets, who had warned them in order to turn them back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and they committed great blasphemies.

L.26: And they were disobedient and rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and threw {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law behind their back, and they killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets, who had warned them to bring them back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; and they did great blasphemies.

R.26: But they disobeyed and turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They turned their backs on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law. They killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets, who had warned them to come back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They did terrible things that insulted {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: threw your law behind their back: treated it with contempt
decisions.reason: To throw something behind one's back is to reject it and put it out of mind (1 Kings 14:9; Ezekiel 23:35).

decisions.choice: they killed your prophets: 1 Kings 18:4; 19:10; 2 Chronicles 24:20-22; Jeremiah 26:20-23
decisions.reason: The books of Kings, Chronicles and Jeremiah record prophets put to death: Jezebel killed the prophets of the LORD (1 Kings 18:4; 19:10), Zechariah son of Jehoiada was stoned in the temple court (2 Chronicles 24:20-22), and King Jehoiakim had Uriah killed (Jeremiah 26:20-23).

decisions.choice: warned: testified against them
decisions.reason: The verb means to bear witness, to warn solemnly (2 Kings 17:13, 15). It returns in verses 29, 30 and 34.

decisions.choice: terrible things that insulted you
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, Readable explains "blasphemies" by saying whom they scorned.

records.source: וַֽתִּתְּנֵם֙ בְּיַ֣ד צָֽרֵיהֶ֔ם וַיָּצֵ֖רוּ לָהֶ֑ם וּבְעֵ֤ת צָֽרָתָם֙ יִצְעֲק֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּה֙ מִשָּׁמַ֣יִם תִּשְׁמָ֔ע וּֽכְרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֗ים תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעִ֔ים וְיוֹשִׁיע֖וּם מִיַּ֥ד צָרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you gave them into [the] hand of their adversaries, and they distressed them; and in [the] time of their distress they cried out to you, and you from heaven heard, and according to your compassions the great you gave them saviors, and they saved them from [the] hand of their adversaries.
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. But in the time of their distress they cried out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} heard from heaven, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them deliverers who rescued them from the power of their enemies.

L.27: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they distressed them. And in the time of their distress they cried out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} heard from heaven, and according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them saviors, and they saved them from the hand of their adversaries.

R.27: So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} handed them over to their enemies, who made them suffer. When they were suffering, they cried out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You heard them from heaven. Because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mercy is so great, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent them leaders who rescued them from their enemies.

decisions.choice: given to enemies, crying out, saviors raised up: the pattern of the book of Judges
decisions.reason: The prayer sums up the cycle told in Judges: Israel sinned, the LORD gave them into the hand of their enemies, they cried out, and he raised up deliverers who saved them (Judges 2:14-18; 3:9, 15). The word for "saviors" is the one used there of Othniel and Ehud.

decisions.choice: the hand of: the power of
decisions.reason: "The hand" of an enemy means his power and control (verse 24).

decisions.choice: deliverers; leaders who rescued them
decisions.reason: Balanced says "deliverers" and Readable "leaders who rescued them", since "savior" in English is used mostly of God and Christ; Literal keeps "saviors".

records.source: וּכְנ֣וֹחַ לָהֶ֔ם יָשׁ֕וּבוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רַ֖ע לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַתַּֽעַזְבֵ֞ם בְּיַ֤ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְדּ֣וּ בָהֶ֔ם וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ וַיִּזְעָק֔וּךָ וְאַתָּ֞ה מִשָּׁמַ֧יִם תִּשְׁמַ֛ע וְתַצִּילֵ֥ם כְּֽרַחֲמֶ֖יךָ רַבּ֥וֹת עִתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And when [there was] rest to them, they returned to do evil before you, and you left them in [the] hand of their enemies, and they ruled over them; and they returned and cried out to you, and you from heaven heard and rescued them according to your compassions, many times.
pieces: But as soon as they had rest, they again did evil in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} abandoned them to their enemies, who ruled over them. When they cried out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} again, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} heard from heaven, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rescued them many times.

L.28: But when they had rest, they again did evil before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} left them in the hand of their enemies, and they ruled over them. And they again cried out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} heard from heaven and rescued them according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion, many times.

R.28: But as soon as things were calm, they did evil again in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} left them in the power of their enemies, who ruled over them. Then they cried out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} again, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} heard them from heaven. Because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mercy, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rescued them again and again.

decisions.choice: they returned to do evil; they returned and cried out: they did it again
decisions.reason: "Returned to" with another verb means doing it again (Judges 3:12; 4:1). The second "returned" may also hint at turning back to God; the plain sense is that they cried out again.

decisions.choice: many times: the rescue happened again and again
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the end and sums up the whole cycle: God's rescue came not once but many times (Psalm 106:43).

decisions.choice: before you: in your sight
decisions.reason: To do evil "before" God is to do what he sees and judges evil (Judges 2:11).

records.source: וַתָּ֨עַד בָּהֶ֜ם לַהֲשִׁיבָ֣ם אֶל־תּוֹרָתֶ֗ךָ וְהֵ֨מָּה הֵזִ֜ידוּ וְלֹא־שָׁמְע֤וּ לְמִצְוֺתֶ֨יךָ֙ וּבְמִשְׁפָּטֶ֣יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־בָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֖ם וְחָיָ֣ה בָהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ כָתֵף֙ סוֹרֶ֔רֶת וְעָרְפָּ֥ם הִקְשׁ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And you warned them to bring them back to your law, and they acted presumptuously and did not listen to your commandments, and against your judgments they sinned, which a man shall do and live by them; and they gave a shoulder stubborn, and their neck they stiffened, and did not listen.
pieces: You warned them in order to turn them back to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law, yet they acted arrogantly and would not obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments. They sinned against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings, by which anyone who keeps them will live. They turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks and would not obey.

L.29: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} warned them, to bring them back to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law; but they acted presumptuously and did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments, and they sinned against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments, which, if a {{gender:person|man}} does them, he will live by them; and they gave a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck and did not listen.

R.29: You warned them to come back to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law. But they were proud and did not obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands. They sinned against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rules, even though anyone who obeys them will live. They turned away stubbornly, refused to bend and would not listen.

decisions.choice: which a person shall do and live by them: Leviticus 18:5
decisions.reason: The words quote Leviticus 18:5: the LORD's statutes and rulings, "which a person shall do and live by them". Ezekiel uses the same words for Israel's rebellion in the wilderness (Ezekiel 20:11, 13, 21). To live by them means to have life, the good life God gives in the land, by keeping them.

decisions.choice: gave a stubborn shoulder: refused the yoke
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox or heifer that pulls its shoulder away from the yoke (Hosea 4:16; Zechariah 7:11). With "stiffened their neck" (verse 16) it says Israel refused to be led.

decisions.choice: warned: testified against them
decisions.reason: As in verse 26, the verb means to warn solemnly, bearing witness against someone.

decisions.choice: a person / a man
decisions.reason: The word means any human being, man or woman; Literal uses the gender setting and Balanced and Readable say "anyone". "He" in Literal follows the Hebrew verb.

records.source: וַתִּמְשֹׁ֤ךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ שָׁנִ֣ים רַבּ֔וֹת וַתָּ֨עַד בָּ֧ם בְּרוּחֲךָ֛ בְּיַד־נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א הֶאֱזִ֑ינוּ וַֽתִּתְּנֵ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד עַמֵּ֥י הָאֲרָצֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And you drew out over them years many, and you warned them by your Spirit by [the] hand of your prophets, and they did not give ear; and you gave them into [the] hand of [the] peoples of the lands.
pieces: For many years {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were patient with them, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} warned them by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Spirit through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets. But they would not listen, so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.

L.30: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bore with them many years and warned them by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Spirit through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets, but they did not give ear; so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.

R.30: For many years {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were patient with them. By {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Spirit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} warned them through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets, but they would not listen. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} handed them over to the nations around them.

decisions.choice: drew out over them many years: bore with them patiently for many years
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw out or prolong. With "over them" it means God held out his patience toward them for a long time (compare Psalm 36:11, "draw out your steadfast love"). The "many years" are the centuries of the kings.

decisions.choice: by your Spirit through your prophets
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke by God's Spirit (Zechariah 7:12, "the words that the LORD of hosts sent by his Spirit through the former prophets"; 2 Samuel 23:2).

decisions.choice: the peoples of the lands: the foreign nations, Assyria and Babylon
decisions.reason: The phrase means the nations outside Israel. The northern kingdom fell to Assyria (2 Kings 17:6) and Judah to Babylon (2 Kings 25:1-21).

decisions.choice: were patient with them; bore with them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the picture "drew out over them"; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וּֽבְרַחֲמֶ֧יךָ הָרַבִּ֛ים לֹֽא־עֲשִׂיתָ֥ם כָּלָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א עֲזַבְתָּ֑ם כִּ֛י אֵֽל־חַנּ֥וּן וְרַח֖וּם אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: And in your compassions the great you did not make them an end and did not forsake them, for a God gracious and compassionate [are] you.
pieces: Yet in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not put an end to them or abandon them, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a gracious and compassionate God.

L.31: But in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not make an end of them and did not forsake them, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] a gracious and compassionate God.

R.31: But because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mercy is so great, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not destroy them completely or leave them. You are a kind and merciful God.

decisions.choice: you did not make a full end of them: Jeremiah 4:27; 5:10, 18
decisions.reason: Even when he judged Judah by Babylon, the LORD said through Jeremiah, "I will not make a full end" (Jeremiah 4:27; 5:18; 30:11). The returned exiles are the proof that he kept his word.

decisions.choice: a gracious and compassionate God: Exodus 34:6
decisions.reason: The prayer comes back to the words of verse 17, God's own description of himself (Exodus 34:6).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱ֠לֹהֵינוּ הָאֵ֨ל הַגָּד֜וֹל הַגִּבּ֣וֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא֮ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַבְּרִ֣ית וְהַחֶסֶד֒ אַל־יִמְעַ֣ט לְפָנֶ֡יךָ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַתְּלָאָ֣ה אֲֽשֶׁר־מְ֠צָאַתְנוּ לִמְלָכֵ֨ינוּ לְשָׂרֵ֧ינוּ וּלְכֹהֲנֵ֛ינוּ וְלִנְבִיאֵ֥נוּ וְלַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ וּלְכָל־עַמֶּ֑ךָ מִימֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And now, our God, the God the great, the mighty and the awesome, keeping the covenant and the steadfast love, let not be small before you all the hardship which has found us, our kings, our princes, and our priests and our prophets and our fathers and all your people, from [the] days of [the] kings of Assyria until the day the this.
pieces: So now, our God, the great, mighty and awesome God, who keeps covenant and faithful love, do not treat as small before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all the hardship that has come upon us, upon our kings, our officials, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors and all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.

L.32: And now, our God, the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who keeps the covenant and steadfast love, do not let all the hardship seem small before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that has come upon us, upon our kings, our princes, and our priests and our prophets and our fathers and all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.

R.32: So now, our God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the great God, mighty and awesome. You keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant and show faithful love. Do not think lightly of all the suffering that has come on us, on our kings and leaders, our priests and prophets, our ancestors and all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. It has gone on from the time of the kings of Assyria until today.

decisions.choice: the great, mighty and awesome God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love: Deuteronomy 10:17; 7:9
decisions.reason: The titles come from Deuteronomy 10:17, and "keeps covenant and steadfast love" from Deuteronomy 7:9. Nehemiah's own prayer begins with the same words (1:5; compare Daniel 9:4). The prayer now turns from the past to the present and makes its request.

decisions.choice: let it not be small before you: do not count it as a small thing
decisions.reason: The request is that God would not treat the people's suffering as unimportant, but take note of it. It is the one plea of the whole prayer; it asks for no particular act, but leaves the answer to God.

decisions.choice: from the days of the kings of Assyria
decisions.reason: Assyria first made Israel pay tribute and then took the northern kingdom into exile in the eighth century BC (2 Kings 15:19, 29; 17:3-6). From then on the people had lived under one foreign empire after another: Assyria, Babylon and now Persia.

decisions.choice: officials; leaders
decisions.reason: Following the term table for this word: Literal "princes", Balanced "officials", Readable "leaders".

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה צַדִּ֔יק עַ֖ל כָּל־הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־אֱמֶ֥ת עָשִׂ֖יתָ וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And you [are] righteous in all that has come upon us, for faithfulness you have done, and we have acted wickedly.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been righteous in all that has come upon us; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have acted faithfully, while we have done wrong.

L.33: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] righteous in all that has come upon us, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have acted faithfully, and we have acted wickedly.

R.33: You have been righteous in everything that has happened to us. You have always been faithful, but we have done wrong.

decisions.choice: you are righteous in all that has come upon us: God is in the right in his judgment
decisions.reason: The prayer does not blame God for the people's suffering. It confesses that God was right to bring it, as Ezra's prayer does (Ezra 9:15) and as Daniel's does (Daniel 9:7, 14).

decisions.choice: faithfulness you have done: you have acted faithfully
decisions.reason: The word means firmness, faithfulness, truth. God has been true to his covenant, both in its blessings and in its warnings (Deuteronomy 28).

decisions.choice: while we have done wrong
decisions.reason: Balanced sets the two halves against each other with "while", as the Hebrew word order ("you ... and we") does.

records.source: וְאֶת־מְלָכֵ֤ינוּ שָׂרֵ֨ינוּ֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣ינוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ לֹ֥א עָשׂ֖וּ תּוֹרָתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹ֤א הִקְשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ אֶל־מִצְוֺתֶ֔יךָ וּלְעֵ֣דְוֺתֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַעִידֹ֖תָ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And our kings, our princes, our priests, and our fathers did not do your law, and did not pay attention to your commandments and to your testimonies which you warned them.
pieces: Our kings, our officials, our priests and our ancestors did not keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law or pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments and the decrees by which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} warned them.

L.34: And our kings, our princes, our priests and our fathers did not do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law and did not pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies with which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} warned them.

R.34: Our kings and leaders, our priests and our ancestors did not obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law. They paid no attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands or to the instructions {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them as a warning.

decisions.choice: your testimonies which you warned them: the solemn decrees that warned them
decisions.reason: "Testimonies" and "warned" come from the same root, to bear witness. God's decrees were a witness set before Israel, warning them what keeping and breaking the covenant would bring (Deuteronomy 4:45; 2 Kings 17:15).

decisions.choice: kings, princes, priests and fathers: the leaders and the whole people
decisions.reason: The list repeats verse 32 without the prophets, who had warned the others. The confession takes in every rank of the people.

decisions.choice: decrees; instructions
decisions.reason: Following the term table: Literal "testimonies", Balanced "decrees", Readable "instructions".

records.source: וְהֵ֣ם בְּמַלְכוּתָם֩ וּבְטוּבְךָ֨ הָרָ֜ב אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֣תָּ לָהֶ֗ם וּבְאֶ֨רֶץ הָרְחָבָ֧ה וְהַשְּׁמֵנָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תָּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א עֲבָד֑וּךָ וְֽלֹא־שָׁ֔בוּ מִמַּֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֖ם הָרָעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they, in their kingdom and in your goodness the great which you gave to them, and in the land the broad and the fat which you set before them, did not serve you and did not turn back from their deeds the evil.
pieces: Even in their own kingdom, with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great goodness that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them, and in the broad and fertile land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set before them, they did not serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} or turn from their evil deeds.

L.35: And they, in their own kingdom and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great goodness that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them, and in the broad and fat land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set before them, did not serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and did not turn back from their evil deeds.

R.35: Even when they had their own kingdom, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were so good to them, and when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them a large and rich land, they did not serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They did not turn away from the evil things they were doing.

decisions.choice: they, in their own kingdom: while Israel was still an independent kingdom
decisions.reason: "Their kingdom" sets the time of the kings, when Israel ruled itself, against the present, when it is under foreign rule (verses 36-37). Even with every advantage, the people did not serve God.

decisions.choice: the broad and fat land: Exodus 3:8
decisions.reason: The land was described to Moses as "a good and broad land, a land flowing with milk and honey" (Exodus 3:8). "Fat" means fertile, as in verse 25.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ הַיּ֖וֹם עֲבָדִ֑ים וְהָאָ֜רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֣תָּה לַאֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־פִּרְיָהּ֙ וְאֶת־טוּבָ֔הּ הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֲבָדִ֖ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Look, we [are] today slaves, and the land which you gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good, look, we [are] slaves on it.
pieces: See, we are slaves today, slaves in the very land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave our ancestors so that they could eat its fruit and enjoy its good things.

L.36: See, we are slaves today; and the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good things, see, we are slaves in it.

R.36: Look at us now! We are slaves today. We are slaves in the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave our ancestors so they could eat its fruit and enjoy its good things.

decisions.choice: we are slaves: under Persian rule
decisions.reason: The people were subjects of the Persian king. They paid him tribute and taxes (Ezra 4:13, 20; Nehemiah 5:4) and the land's produce went to him (verse 37). Ezra 9:9 says the same: "we are slaves, yet our God has not forsaken us in our slavery". The prayer sets this against the purpose of the gift of the land: that Israel should eat its fruit as free people.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: The point is the loss of freedom set against the gift of the land, so the word stays "slaves" at every level, as the style guide asks where slavery itself is the point.

decisions.choice: See; Look
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word calls attention to what follows. It is rendered "See" or "Look", not "behold", by the project's rule.

records.source: וּתְבוּאָתָ֣הּ מַרְבָּ֗ה לַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תָּה עָלֵ֖ינוּ בְּחַטֹּאותֵ֑ינוּ וְעַ֣ל גְּ֠וִיֹּתֵינוּ מֹשְׁלִ֤ים וּבִבְהֶמְתֵּ֨נוּ֙ כִּרְצוֹנָ֔ם וּבְצָרָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And its produce [is] multiplying for the kings whom you have set over us in our sins; and over our bodies [they are] ruling and over our cattle according to their will, and in distress great [are] we.
pieces: Its rich produce goes to the kings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and over our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress."

L.37: And its abundant produce [goes] to the kings whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set over us because of our sins; and they rule over our bodies and over our livestock as they please, and we [are] in great distress."

R.37: The rich harvest of this land goes to the kings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have put over us because of our sins. They rule over us and over our animals and do whatever they like. We are in great trouble."

decisions.choice: its produce increases for the kings: the harvest goes to the Persian king in taxes
decisions.reason: The land is fruitful, but its yield goes in tribute to the foreign king (Ezra 4:13; Nehemiah 5:4, 15). Moses had warned that this would happen if Israel forsook the LORD (Deuteronomy 28:33, 51).

decisions.choice: they rule over our bodies: they can command our persons
decisions.reason: The Persian king could call men for labor or for war and took the people's animals for his use, as he pleased. "Bodies" means the people themselves.

decisions.choice: in our sins: because of our sins
decisions.reason: The preposition here gives the reason: the foreign kings rule because of Israel's sins, as the whole prayer has confessed.

decisions.choice: and we are in great distress: the prayer ends
decisions.reason: The prayer ends here with no closing praise, only the people's need laid before God. The next verse (10:1) tells what they did about it: they made a firm written agreement.

decisions.choice: rule over us
decisions.reason: Readable says "us" for "our bodies", which the meaning decision explains.
